8	/-!
9	# The Čech Euler characteristic is an inclusion–exclusion count — unconditionally
10	
11	Every χ-statement in this lane so far has been *gated*: `ChiLedger.chi_add` and its
12	descendants take four exactness hypotheses (`window`, `connect`, `twist`, and the
13	surjectivity `htwist`) packaging the ledger four-term sequence
14	`0 → L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D) → Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D') → 0`, whose connecting map and
15	right-exactness the lane does not construct.  That is why `hbump` — "χ jumps by
16	`[κ(P):k]` at every one-point bump" — has been carried as an open hypothesis, and why
17	the audit at inbox `I-0449` was able to *refute* it off the cover overlap.
18	
19	This file removes the gate for the underlying numerical identity.  The point is that
20	for a **two-set cover** the Čech Euler characteristic needs no exact sequence at all:
21	
22	`χ(D) = dim 𝒞⁰(D) − dim 𝒞¹(D)` where `𝒞⁰(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) ⊕ Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))`,
23	`𝒞¹(D) = 𝒜(D) = Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁, 𝒪(D))`,
24	
25	and both `ℓ(D) = dim ker` and `h¹(D) = dim coker` are read off the *same* map by
26	rank–nullity.  Concretely, with `B(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))` the coboundary and
27	`L(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) ⊓ Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))` the global sections (`Substrate.linearSystem_eq_inf`
28	on a cover), the modular law
29	`dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) = dim S₀ + dim S₁`
30	(mathlib's `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`) *is* the Euler characteristic:
31	
32	`χ(D) = ℓ(D) − h¹(D) = dim L(D) − (dim 𝒜(D) − dim B(D))`
33	      `= dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) − dim 𝒜(D) = dim S₀ + dim S₁ − dim 𝒜(D)`.
34	
35	## What is proved, and what it is worth
36	
37	* `chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` — **the unconditional χ formula.**
38	  `χ(D) = dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim 𝒜(D)` on a cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`,
39	  with **no exactness hypotheses** — only the finiteness of the two chart section
40	  spaces.  This is strictly stronger than what `chi_add` gives, in the precise sense
41	  that it has none of `chi_add`'s four gated binders.
42	
43	* `chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` — the difference form: the χ-jump between two
44	  divisors is an alternating sum of three *local step* dimensions, again unconditionally.
45	
46	* `chi_add_of_charts` — **gate-free χ-additivity.**  `χ(D') = χ(D) + (local overlap step)`
47	  precisely when the two chart steps vanish.  Compare `ChiLedger.chi_add`, which reaches
48	  the same conclusion from four exactness hypotheses: this version replaces all four by a
49	  *checkable* condition on the two charts.
50	
51	* `chi_add_eq_residueDeg_of_charts` — the one-point bump with the residue degree, from
52	  the chart condition plus strong approximation (`hsurj`), no exactness gate.
53	
54	* `chi_add_of_notMem_overlap` — **`χ` is constant across an off-overlap bump, and this
55	  is now a THEOREM, not a refutation of a hypothesis.**  Where `I-0449`'s
56	  `not_bump_of_notMem_overlap` derived a contradiction *from* `chi_add`'s hypotheses
57	  (a conditional refutation), this proves `χ(1·P + E) = χ(E)` outright.  Consequently:
58	
59	* `not_bump_of_notMem_overlap_unconditional` — `hbump` is **unconditionally false** at
60	  every off-overlap prime, on every curve with a nonempty off-overlap prime and finite
61	  chart sections.  This is the sharp form the audit at `I-0456` asked for ("WHERE is H
62	  false?") and it settles the status of `hbump`: it is not merely unproved off the
63	  overlap, it is refutable there, so `chi_eq_of_bump` must not be advertised as the
64	  ledger's route.  See §4 for what survives.
65	
66	## Provenance
67	
68	Rederived in AJC's own abstractions (`sectionSub`, `chi`, `H1Mod`).  This is **not** a
69	port: the sibling project's `RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean` core is a bounded
70	vanishing statement, not this identity, and nothing of this shape existed in either
71	project — the lane had only the gated `chi_add`.  The mathlib input is exactly one
72	lemma, `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`.
73	-/

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.LedgerClosure
7	
8	/-!
9	# The Čech Euler characteristic is an inclusion–exclusion count — unconditionally
10	
11	Every χ-statement in this lane so far has been *gated*: `ChiLedger.chi_add` and its
12	descendants take four exactness hypotheses (`window`, `connect`, `twist`, and the
13	surjectivity `htwist`) packaging the ledger four-term sequence
14	`0 → L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D) → Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D') → 0`, whose connecting map and
15	right-exactness the lane does not construct.  That is why `hbump` — "χ jumps by
16	`[κ(P):k]` at every one-point bump" — has been carried as an open hypothesis, and why
17	the audit at inbox `I-0449` was able to *refute* it off the cover overlap.
18	
19	This file removes the gate for the underlying numerical identity.  The point is that
20	for a **two-set cover** the Čech Euler characteristic needs no exact sequence at all:
21	
22	`χ(D) = dim 𝒞⁰(D) − dim 𝒞¹(D)` where `𝒞⁰(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) ⊕ Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))`,
23	`𝒞¹(D) = 𝒜(D) = Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁, 𝒪(D))`,
24	
25	and both `ℓ(D) = dim ker` and `h¹(D) = dim coker` are read off the *same* map by
26	rank–nullity.  Concretely, with `B(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))` the coboundary and
27	`L(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) ⊓ Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))` the global sections (`Substrate.linearSystem_eq_inf`
28	on a cover), the modular law
29	`dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) = dim S₀ + dim S₁`
30	(mathlib's `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`) *is* the Euler characteristic:
31	
32	`χ(D) = ℓ(D) − h¹(D) = dim L(D) − (dim 𝒜(D) − dim B(D))`
33	      `= dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) − dim 𝒜(D) = dim S₀ + dim S₁ − dim 𝒜(D)`.
34	
35	## What is proved, and what it is worth
36	
37	* `chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` — **the unconditional χ formula.**
38	  `χ(D) = dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim 𝒜(D)` on a cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`,
39	  with **no exactness hypotheses** — only the finiteness of the two chart section
40	  spaces.  This is strictly stronger than what `chi_add` gives, in the precise sense
41	  that it has none of `chi_add`'s four gated binders.
42	
43	* `chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` — the difference form: the χ-jump between two
44	  divisors is an alternating sum of three *local step* dimensions, again unconditionally.
45	
46	* `chi_add_of_charts` — **gate-free χ-additivity.**  `χ(D') = χ(D) + (local overlap step)`
47	  precisely when the two chart steps vanish.  Compare `ChiLedger.chi_add`, which reaches
48	  the same conclusion from four exactness hypotheses: this version replaces all four by a
49	  *checkable* condition on the two charts.
50	
51	* `chi_add_eq_residueDeg_of_charts` — the one-point bump with the residue degree, from
52	  the chart condition plus strong approximation (`hsurj`), no exactness gate.
53	
54	* `chi_add_of_notMem_overlap` — **`χ` is constant across an off-overlap bump, and this
55	  is now a THEOREM, not a refutation of a hypothesis.**  Where `I-0449`'s
56	  `not_bump_of_notMem_overlap` derived a contradiction *from* `chi_add`'s hypotheses
57	  (a conditional refutation), this proves `χ(1·P + E) = χ(E)` outright.  Consequently:
58	
59	* `not_bump_of_notMem_overlap_unconditional` — `hbump` is **unconditionally false** at
60	  every off-overlap prime, on every curve with a nonempty off-overlap prime and finite
61	  chart sections.  This is the sharp form the audit at `I-0456` asked for ("WHERE is H
62	  false?") and it settles the status of `hbump`: it is not merely unproved off the
63	  overlap, it is refutable there, so `chi_eq_of_bump` must not be advertised as the
64	  ledger's route.  See §4 for what survives.
65	
66	## Provenance
67	
68	Rederived in AJC's own abstractions (`sectionSub`, `chi`, `H1Mod`).  This is **not** a
69	port: the sibling project's `RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean` core is a bounded
70	vanishing statement, not this identity, and nothing of this shape existed in either
71	project — the lane had only the gated `chi_add`.  The mathlib input is exactly one
72	lemma, `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`.
73	-/

102	
103	`χ(D) = dim_k Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim_k Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim_k 𝒜(D)`.

105	**No exactness hypotheses.**  The only inputs are the cover and the finiteness of the two
106	chart section spaces; `𝒜(D)`'s finiteness follows, since `𝒜(D) ⊇ B(D)` is not needed —
107	what is needed is that `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D)/B(D)` is finite-dimensional, which is the binder
108	`Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)`.
109	
110	Proof: `ℓ(D) = dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁)` (the cover, `sectionSub_top_eq_inf`) and
111	`h¹(D) = dim 𝒜(D) − dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁)` (rank–nullity for the quotient `𝒜(D)/B(D)`), so
112	`χ(D) = dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) − dim 𝒜(D)`, and the modular law
113	`Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq` replaces the first two terms by
114	`dim S₀ + dim S₁`. -/
115	theorem chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor)
116	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
117	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)] :
118	    chi k U₀ U₁ D = (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
119	      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
120	      - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) := by
121	  classical
122	  -- `h¹(D) + dim B(D) = dim 𝒜(D)`: rank–nullity for `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D) / B(D)`.
123	  have hcob : Module.finrank k (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)
124	      + Module.finrank k (Submodule.comap (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype
125	          (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D))
126	        = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) :=
127	    Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank _
128	  -- The comap of `B(D)` into `𝒜(D)` has the same dimension as `B(D)` itself,
129	  -- because `B(D) ≤ 𝒜(D)`.
130	  have hBeq : Module.finrank k (Submodule.comap (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype
131	      (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D)) = Module.finrank k (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D) :=
132	    (Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe (coboundarySub_le_overlap k U₀ U₁ D)).finrank_eq
133	  -- The modular law for the two chart subspaces.
134	  have hmod : Module.finrank k (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D)
135	      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D : Submodule k X.functionField)
136	        = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D) :=
137	    Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq _ _
138	  -- `ℓ(D) = dim (S₀ ⊓ S₁)` by the cover.
139	  have hell : ell k D
140	      = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D : Submodule k X.functionField) := by
141	    rw [ell, sectionSub_top_eq_inf k U₀ U₁ hcov D]
142	  rw [hBeq] at hcob
143	  simp only [chi, h1dim, hell]
144	  omega
145	
146	/-- **The unconditional χ-difference formula.**  The χ-jump between any two divisors is
147	the alternating sum of the two chart steps and the overlap step:
148	
149	`χ(D') − χ(D) = ΔS₀ + ΔS₁ − Δ𝒜`
150	
151	where each `Δ` is the difference of the corresponding dimensions.  Again no exactness
152	hypotheses.  This is the honest replacement for `ChiLedger.chi_add`. -/
153	theorem chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D D' : X.WeilDivisor)
154	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
155	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
156	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D')] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D')]
157	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D')] :

universe u
open AlgebraicGeometry Adelic

    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

finiteness binders and chi_add's conclusion, the U₁-chart step is 0 off U₀,
hence the bump fails.  So the new formula does not exonerate hbump. -/
theorem i0449_survives (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ E)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ E)]
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E)]
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ (pointDivisor P + E))]
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E))]
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) (pointDivisor P + E))]
    (hchiAdd : chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E
      + Module.finrank k (localStepDom k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E (pointDivisor P + E))) :
    (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E)) : ℤ)
        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ E) = 0
    ∧ chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) ≠ chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P := by
  have hPinf : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens) := fun h => hP h.1
  have hz := finrank_localStepDom_eq_zero_of_notMem_overlap k U₀ U₁ hPinf E
  have h := chi_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_left k U₀ U₁ hcov hP E
  have h1 : 1 ≤ residueDeg k P := one_le_residueDeg k P
  rw [hz] at hchiAdd
  refine ⟨by omega, by omega⟩

`U₀`-chart finiteness is the *global* (lane-standard) finiteness has no instance of
`chi_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_left`. -/

  hP trivial

theorem degenerate_collapse (D : X.WeilDivisor)
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (⊤ : X.Opens) D)] :
    chi k (⊤ : X.Opens) (⊤ : X.Opens) D = (ell k D : ℤ) := by
  have h := chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k (⊤ : X.Opens) (⊤ : X.Opens) (by simp) D
  rw [ell]

theorem old_from_new {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens))
    (E : X.WeilDivisor) :
    sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) (pointDivisor P + E) = sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E :=

  rcases h with h0 | h0
  · exact one_ne_zero h0

    norm_num at h0

/-- **The residue degree is positive**: `1 ≤ [κ(P):k]`.  From the nontriviality of
`κ(P)` (`nontrivial_localStepTgt_one`) plus finite-dimensionality — a nontrivial
finite-dimensional space has positive rank.  Needed wherever a *nonzero* effective
divisor must be given *positive* degree. -/
theorem one_le_residueDeg (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] : 1 ≤ residueDeg k P := by
  haveI := nontrivial_localStepTgt_one k P
  rw [residueDeg, Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero]
  intro h
  exact (not_subsingleton (localStepTgt k P 1))
    ((Module.finrank_zero_iff (R := k)).mp h)

/-- **A nonzero effective divisor has positive weighted degree.**  Some coefficient
`D(P₀)` is `≥ 1` (it is nonzero and `≥ 0`) and contributes `D(P₀)·[κ(P₀):k] ≥ 1`

/-!
# Adelic Riemann–Roch — closing the ledger from the one-point bump

Every conditional statement of the vanishing and generation lane
(`Adelic/SectionBounds.lean` §3, `Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean`,
`Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean`) takes the **closed ledger**

`hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`

as a hypothesis quantified over **all** Weil divisors.  `chi_telescope_list` establishes
it for *effective* divisors from the one-point bump, and the sibling docstrings recorded
"extending from list-effective divisors to all divisors additionally needs the negative
part" as an open item.

**This file closes that extension.**  `chi_eq_of_bump` proves the ledger at every Weil
divisor from the one-point bump alone, so `hledger` is not an independent open input of the
lane: every consumer that takes it can instead take `hbump`.  But `hbump` is
NOT merely one application of `chi_add_eq_residueDeg` per step: that theorem
requires `P.point ∈ U₀ ⊓ U₁`, and off the overlap the lane proves the *negation* of the
bump (`LedgerClosure.not_bump_of_notMem_overlap`), so `hbump` over all primes is strictly
stronger than the exact sequence plus strong approximation.  See §5.

## What is proved

* `chi_eq_of_bump_of_nonneg` — the ledger at **every effective divisor**, with the list
  eliminated from the statement (every effective divisor is list-effective,
  `exists_divisorOfList_of_nonneg`, so a consumer no longer has to produce a list).
* `chi_telescope_list_add` — the telescope run from an **arbitrary base divisor**, not
  only from `0`.
* `chi_eq_of_bump` — **the closed ledger, at every Weil divisor**, from the bump alone.

## The negative part costs nothing, and why this file previously said otherwise

An earlier version of this module — and the sibling docstrings in `SectionBounds.lean`,
`BoundedVanishing.lean` and `ResidueField.lean` — recorded the extension from the effective
cone to all divisors as **open**, "needing an input the lane does not have".  That was
false, and the error is worth stating precisely, because it survived three sessions and
shaped their plans.

The reasoning was: write `D = D⁺ − (−D)⁺` as a difference of effective divisors; the
effective case handles each piece; but `χ` is **not additive** in the divisor, and `D` is
**not linearly equivalent** to `D⁺` in general, so neither of the lane's two transport
mechanisms moves `χ` across the decomposition.  Every clause of that is true — and
irrelevant, because no transport is needed.  `hbump` is quantified over **every** base
divisor `E`, not only over effective ones, so the telescope is not confined to the effective
cone: read the same identity as `D⁺ = (−D)⁺ + D`, i.e. the effective divisor `(−D)⁺`
telescoped **onto the base `D`**, and `chi_telescope_list_add` computes `χ(D⁺)` from `χ(D)`
in one induction.  Comparing with the effective-cone value of `χ(D⁺)` gives the ledger at
`D`.

The generalisable lesson: the obstruction was sought among the *transports* the lane owns,
when what mattered was the *quantifier* of a hypothesis the lane already had.

mathematical expectation about the intended covers, **not** a theorem in this file: the lemmas
below hold for arbitrary `U₀ U₁`, where the exceptional set may be large or everything.)

theorem finrank_localStepDom_eq_zero_of_notMem_overlap
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens)) (E : X.WeilDivisor) :

    constructor

    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ b
    rw [Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply]

/-- **`hbump` is REFUTED at every off-overlap prime, by the lane's own ledger exact sequence.**

This is the sharpest thing to know about `hbump`, and it corrects the cost accounting that five
docstrings in this lane carried (including this file's).  Those said each instance of `hbump` is
"one application of `ChiLedger.chi_add_eq_residueDeg`".  **False off the overlap**, twice over:

* `chi_add_eq_residueDeg` carries `hPV : P.point ∈ U₀ ⊓ U₁`, so at an off-overlap `P` the lane

sequence plus strong approximation, one prime at a time": it additionally forces `chi_add`'s
window/connect/twist exactness hypotheses to *fail* at every off-overlap one-point step.  Since
a 2-affine cover of a proper curve has `U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≠ ⊤`, that exceptional set is nonempty for the
covers of interest.

correct: from `hbump` the ledger follows at every divisor.  What it changes is how `hbump` should

consumer intending to discharge `hbump` from `chi_add_eq_residueDeg` **cannot**, and this theorem

    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens)) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
    (hchiAdd : chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E
      + Module.finrank k (localStepDom k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E (pointDivisor P + E))) :
    chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) ≠ chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P := by
  rw [finrank_localStepDom_eq_zero_of_notMem_overlap k U₀ U₁ hP E] at hchiAdd

  omega

    ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),

  fun P _ => isEmptyElim P

250	/-! ## §3. Cluster-P consequences that no longer need the ledger
251	
252	The two statements cluster P actually wants downstream are a **section lower bound**
253	(Riemann inequality) and an **H¹ vanishing criterion**.  Both follow from the ungated χ
254	formula without `hledger`, `hbump`, or any exactness hypothesis.  What they still need is
255	the *geometric* input relating the chart dimensions to `deg D`; that input is isolated as
256	an explicit hypothesis rather than hidden, and it is the honest residual leaf. -/
257	
258	/-- **Riemann inequality, gate-free.**  `ℓ(D) ≥ χ(D)` is elementary (`chi_le_ell`), so the
259	ungated χ formula turns any lower bound on the Čech count into a lower bound on `ℓ(D)`:
260	
261	`dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim 𝒜(D) ≤ ℓ(D)`.
262	
263	Compare `SectionBounds.degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell` and
264	`BoundedVanishing.exists_bound_ell_eq`, which reach comparable conclusions only under
265	`hledger`.  Here there is no ledger hypothesis at all; the content has moved into the
266	computable left-hand side. -/
267	theorem charts_sub_overlap_le_ell (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor)
268	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
269	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)] :
270	    (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
271	      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
272	      - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) ≤ (ell k D : ℤ) := by
273	  rw [← chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D]
274	  exact chi_le_ell k U₀ U₁ D
275	
276	/-- **H¹ vanishing is equivalent to the Čech count being exact** — no gate.
277	
278	`Ȟ¹(D) = 0` iff `dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim 𝒜(D) = ℓ(D)`, i.e. iff the
279	inclusion–exclusion count computes `ℓ(D)` on the nose.
280	
281	This is the vanishing criterion cluster P needs, and unlike
282	`BoundedVanishing.subsingleton_h1Mod_iff` (a restatement of `𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`) it is a
283	**numerical** criterion: it can be certified by counting dimensions on the two charts,
284	which is what an explicit cover computation actually produces.  Note it is a genuine
285	two-way reduction, not a reformulation of `h1dim = 0` — the right-hand side mentions only
286	the three chart dimensions and `ℓ`. -/
287	theorem h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor)
288	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
289	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)] :
290	    h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0 ↔
291	      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
292	        + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
293	        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = (ell k D : ℤ) := by
294	  have h := chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D
295	  rw [chi] at h
296	  omega
297	
298	/-- **Uniform vanishing from a uniform chart count.**  If above some weighted-degree
299	threshold `b` the Čech count is exact at every divisor, then `h¹` vanishes uniformly above
300	`b`.  The quantifier structure is the one cluster P's consumers take, and the hypothesis is
301	now a statement about chart dimensions rather than about a connecting homomorphism.
302

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.GlobalGeneration

/-!
# Adelic Riemann–Roch — closing the ledger from the one-point bump

Every conditional statement of the vanishing and generation lane
(`Adelic/SectionBounds.lean` §3, `Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean`,
`Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean`) takes the **closed ledger**

`hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`

as a hypothesis quantified over **all** Weil divisors.  `chi_telescope_list` establishes
it for *effective* divisors from the one-point bump, and the sibling docstrings recorded
"extending from list-effective divisors to all divisors additionally needs the negative
part" as an open item.

**This file closes that extension.**  `chi_eq_of_bump` proves the ledger at every Weil
divisor from the one-point bump alone, so `hledger` is not an independent open input of the
lane: every consumer that takes it can instead take `hbump`.  But `hbump` is
NOT merely one application of `chi_add_eq_residueDeg` per step: that theorem
requires `P.point ∈ U₀ ⊓ U₁`, and off the overlap the lane proves the *negation* of the
bump (`LedgerClosure.not_bump_of_notMem_overlap`), so `hbump` over all primes is strictly
stronger than the exact sequence plus strong approximation.  See §5.

## What is proved

* `chi_eq_of_bump_of_nonneg` — the ledger at **every effective divisor**, with the list
  eliminated from the statement (every effective divisor is list-effective,
  `exists_divisorOfList_of_nonneg`, so a consumer no longer has to produce a list).
* `chi_telescope_list_add` — the telescope run from an **arbitrary base divisor**, not
  only from `0`.
* `chi_eq_of_bump` — **the closed ledger, at every Weil divisor**, from the bump alone.

## The negative part costs nothing, and why this file previously said otherwise

An earlier version of this module — and the sibling docstrings in `SectionBounds.lean`,
`BoundedVanishing.lean` and `ResidueField.lean` — recorded the extension from the effective
cone to all divisors as **open**, "needing an input the lane does not have".  That was
false, and the error is worth stating precisely, because it survived three sessions and
shaped their plans.

The reasoning was: write `D = D⁺ − (−D)⁺` as a difference of effective divisors; the
effective case handles each piece; but `χ` is **not additive** in the divisor, and `D` is
**not linearly equivalent** to `D⁺` in general, so neither of the lane's two transport
mechanisms moves `χ` across the decomposition.  Every clause of that is true — and
irrelevant, because no transport is needed.  `hbump` is quantified over **every** base
divisor `E`, not only over effective ones, so the telescope is not confined to the effective
cone: read the same identity as `D⁺ = (−D)⁺ + D`, i.e. the effective divisor `(−D)⁺`
telescoped **onto the base `D`**, and `chi_telescope_list_add` computes `χ(D⁺)` from `χ(D)`
in one induction.  Comparing with the effective-cone value of `χ(D⁺)` gives the ledger at
`D`.

The generalisable lesson: the obstruction was sought among the *transports* the lane owns,
when what mattered was the *quantifier* of a hypothesis the lane already had.

opens of an irreducible curve) the overlap should be a dense open omitting only finitely many
closed points, so the primes disposed of are the few, not the many.  (That estimate is a
mathematical expectation about the intended covers, **not** a theorem in this file: the lemmas
below hold for arbitrary `U₀ U₁`, where the exceptional set may be large or everything.)

But the identity `𝒜(1·P + E) = 𝒜(E)` that makes the peel free off the overlap is the *same*
computation that shows the ledger exact sequence gives a `χ`-jump of `0` there, rather than
`[κ(P):k]`.  So §3's real content is not modesty about a count: it is the evidence that **`hbump`
is refutable at off-overlap primes** — see §5 (`not_bump_of_notMem_overlap`), which turns this
observation into a theorem.  An earlier version of this paragraph offered the diagnosis "one
cannot shrink the exceptional set by choosing a better cover, because it is already nearly
empty", which is true and points away from that.  Credit for the re-reading: an independent
`work-reviewer` audit (inbox I-0450).

What remains at an overlap point is the substantive input: the
Mittag-Leffler/strong-approximation statement that a section with a first-order pole at `P`
can be corrected, modulo the coboundary, by an overlap section without it.  Nothing here
supplies that, and it is the same datum `ChiLedger.localStepMapₖ_surjective` takes as
`hsurj`.  The value of the section is that the residual leaf now has an explicitly bounded
domain of quantification rather than being stated at all primes, and that the two easy cases
are no longer mixed with the hard one.

(These lemmas are about `Peel`, defined in `BoundedVanishing.lean`; they live here because
this file is where the ledger closure makes the peel the residual input.) -/

section PeelOffOverlap

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

/-- **Off the overlap, a one-point bump does not change the overlap sections.**
`𝒜(1·P + E) = 𝒜(E)` when `P.point ∉ U₀ ⊓ U₁`, because the two divisors differ only at `P`
and `𝒜` reads the divisor only at primes meeting the overlap. -/
theorem sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens)) (E : X.WeilDivisor) :
    sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) (pointDivisor P + E) = sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · intro x hx
    rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
    · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    refine Or.inr fun Q hQ => ?_
    have hQP : Q ≠ P := fun h => hP (h ▸ hQ)
    rw [← add_pointDivisor_apply_of_ne E hQP]
    exact ((mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hx0).mp hx) Q hQ
  · exact sectionSub_mono k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) (le_add_pointDivisor E P)

/-- **The one-point peel is free off the overlap.**  For a prime divisor `P` with
`P.point ∉ U₀ ⊓ U₁`, `Peel E (1·P + E)` holds for every `E`, with no approximation input:
take `y = x`, legitimate because the bump did not change the overlap sections
(`sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap`).

So the one-point peel — one of the lane's two residual open inputs — has content **only** at
primes whose point lies in the overlap. -/
theorem peel_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens)) (E : X.WeilDivisor) :
    Peel k U₀ U₁ E (pointDivisor P + E) := by
  intro x hx
  refine ⟨x, ?_, by simp⟩
  rwa [sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap k U₀ U₁ hP E] at hx


What this section does **not** claim: that `hbump` *holds* at any particular curve.  Exhibiting
one needs the strong-approximation input `hsurj`, which is the lane's residual open leaf.  The
distinction between "consistent" and "satisfied somewhere interesting" is the kind this task's
predecessors got wrong in the other direction, so it is stated rather than left to the reader.
The non-degenerate half of the picture is that `ResidueField.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric` produces
an actual prime divisor on a curve, so the vacuous witness does not apply there. -/

section BumpRefuted

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

/-- **Off the overlap the local step is trivial.**  `𝒜(1·P + E) = 𝒜(E)` for `P.point ∉ U₀ ⊓ U₁`
(`sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap`), so the local step space is a subsingleton and
its `k`-dimension is `0`. -/
theorem finrank_localStepDom_eq_zero_of_notMem_overlap
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens)) (E : X.WeilDivisor) :
    Module.finrank k (localStepDom k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E (pointDivisor P + E)) = 0 := by
  have h := sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap k U₀ U₁ hP E
  haveI : Subsingleton (localStepDom k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E (pointDivisor P + E)) := by
    constructor
    intro a b
    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ a
    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ b
    rw [Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply]
    exact Submodule.sub_mem _ (h ▸ x.2) (h ▸ y.2)
  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton

/-- **`hbump` is REFUTED at every off-overlap prime, by the lane's own ledger exact sequence.**

This is the sharpest thing to know about `hbump`, and it corrects the cost accounting that five
docstrings in this lane carried (including this file's).  Those said each instance of `hbump` is
"one application of `ChiLedger.chi_add_eq_residueDeg`".  **False off the overlap**, twice over:

* `chi_add_eq_residueDeg` carries `hPV : P.point ∈ U₀ ⊓ U₁`, so at an off-overlap `P` the lane
  has no route to the bump at all — not even a gated one;
* worse, what the lane *can* prove there is the **negation**.  `chi_add` concludes
  `χ(1·P + E) = χ(E) + dim_k(𝒜(1·P+E)/𝒜(E))`, and off the overlap that dimension is `0`
  (`finrank_localStepDom_eq_zero_of_notMem_overlap`), while `hbump` asserts a jump of
  `[κ(P):k] ≥ 1` (`one_le_residueDeg`).  Hence the conclusion below.

So `hbump` as quantified over **all** primes is strictly stronger than "the ledger exact
sequence plus strong approximation, one prime at a time": it additionally forces `chi_add`'s
window/connect/twist exactness hypotheses to *fail* at every off-overlap one-point step.  Since
a 2-affine cover of a proper curve has `U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≠ ⊤`, that exceptional set is nonempty for the
covers of interest.

**What this does and does not do to `chi_eq_of_bump`.**  It does not touch its proof, which is
correct: from `hbump` the ledger follows at every divisor.  What it changes is how `hbump` should
be read — as a hypothesis satisfiable only in the presence of cohomology data that differs from
`chi_add`'s at off-overlap primes, not as a routine consequence of the exact sequence.  A
consumer intending to discharge `hbump` from `chi_add_eq_residueDeg` **cannot**, and this theorem
is why.

Credit: found by an independent `work-reviewer` audit of this session's work (inbox I-0449 /
I-0451), and machine-checked here rather than left as prose. -/
theorem not_bump_of_notMem_overlap
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens)) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
    (hchiAdd : chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E
      + Module.finrank k (localStepDom k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E (pointDivisor P + E))) :
    chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) ≠ chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P := by
  rw [finrank_localStepDom_eq_zero_of_notMem_overlap k U₀ U₁ hP E] at hchiAdd
  have h1 : 1 ≤ residueDeg k P := one_le_residueDeg k P
  omega

end BumpRefuted

section BumpSatisfiable

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

/-- **`hbump` holds vacuously on a scheme with no prime divisors** — the cheap witness that it
is not a contradictory hypothesis.

This is a *degenerate* witness and is labelled as one: on such a scheme every `∀ P` statement
in the lane is vacuous, and `degK` is identically `0`, so the ledger it yields is the trivial
`χ(D) = χ(0)`.  It establishes exactly one thing — that `hbump` is consistent — and nothing
about the lane's content.

The non-degenerate direction is the other one, and this project has it: `ResidueField`'s
`primeDivisorOfNotGeneric` produces an actual prime divisor on a curve, so on a curve the `∀ P`
quantifier ranges over a nonempty family and the degenerate witness does not apply.  Both facts
together are what "satisfiable and not idle" means. -/
theorem bump_of_isEmpty_primeDivisor [IsEmpty X.PrimeDivisor] :
    ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
      chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P :=
  fun P _ => isEmptyElim P

end BumpSatisfiable

31

33	      `= dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) − dim 𝒜(D) = dim S₀ + dim S₁ − dim 𝒜(D)`.

48	  the same conclusion from four exactness hypotheses: this version replaces all four by a
49	  *checkable* condition on the two charts.

52	  the chart condition plus strong approximation (`hsurj`), no exactness gate.

55	  is now a THEOREM, not a refutation of a hypothesis.**  Where `I-0449`'s
56	  `not_bump_of_notMem_overlap` derived a contradiction *from* `chi_add`'s hypotheses
57	  (a conditional refutation), this proves `χ(1·P + E) = χ(E)` outright.  Consequently:

60	  every off-overlap prime, on every curve with a nonempty off-overlap prime and finite
61	  chart sections.  This is the sharp form the audit at `I-0456` asked for ("WHERE is H
62	  false?") and it settles the status of `hbump`: it is not merely unproved off the
63	  overlap, it is refutable there, so `chi_eq_of_bump` must not be advertised as the
64	  ledger's route.  See §4 for what survives.

71	project — the lane had only the gated `chi_add`.  The mathlib input is exactly one
72	lemma, `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`.

87	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
88	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
89	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
90	
91	/-- **`L(D)` is the intersection of the two chart section spaces**, as `k`-submodules.
92	The `k`-linear form of `Substrate.linearSystem_eq_inf`. -/
93	theorem sectionSub_top_eq_inf (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
94	    sectionSub k ⊤ D = sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D := by
95	  apply SetLike.coe_injective
96	  show (sectionOfDivisor ⊤ D : Set X.functionField) = _
97	  rw [show sectionOfDivisor (X := X) ⊤ D = linearSystem D from rfl,
98	    linearSystem_eq_inf hcov D]
99	  rfl
100	
101	/-- **The unconditional Čech Euler characteristic.**  On a two-set cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`,
102	
103	`χ(D) = dim_k Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim_k Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim_k 𝒜(D)`.
104	
105	**No exactness hypotheses.**  The only inputs are the cover and the finiteness of the two
106	chart section spaces; `𝒜(D)`'s finiteness follows, since `𝒜(D) ⊇ B(D)` is not needed —
107	what is needed is that `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D)/B(D)` is finite-dimensional, which is the binder
108	`Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)`.
109	
110	Proof: `ℓ(D) = dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁)` (the cover, `sectionSub_top_eq_inf`) and
111	`h¹(D) = dim 𝒜(D) − dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁)` (rank–nullity for the quotient `𝒜(D)/B(D)`), so
112	`χ(D) = dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) − dim 𝒜(D)`, and the modular law
113	`Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq` replaces the first two terms by
114	`dim S₀ + dim S₁`. -/
115	theorem chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor)
116	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
117	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)] :
118	    chi k U₀ U₁ D = (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
119	      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
120	      - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) := by
121	  classical
122	  -- `h¹(D) + dim B(D) = dim 𝒜(D)`: rank–nullity for `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D) / B(D)`.
123	  have hcob : Module.finrank k (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)
124	      + Module.finrank k (Submodule.comap (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype
125	          (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D))
126	        = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) :=
127	    Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank _
128	  -- The comap of `B(D)` into `𝒜(D)` has the same dimension as `B(D)` itself,
129	  -- because `B(D) ≤ 𝒜(D)`.
130	  have hBeq : Module.finrank k (Submodule.comap (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype
131	      (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D)) = Module.finrank k (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D) :=
132	    (Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe (coboundarySub_le_overlap k U₀ U₁ D)).finrank_eq
133	  -- The modular law for the two chart subspaces.
134	  have hmod : Module.finrank k (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D)
135	      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D : Submodule k X.functionField)
136	        = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D) :=
137	    Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq _ _
138	  -- `ℓ(D) = dim (S₀ ⊓ S₁)` by the cover.
139	  have hell : ell k D
140	      = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D : Submodule k X.functionField) := by
141	    rw [ell, sectionSub_top_eq_inf k U₀ U₁ hcov D]
142	  rw [hBeq] at hcob
143	  simp only [chi, h1dim, hell]
144	  omega
145	
146	/-- **The unconditional χ-difference formula.**  The χ-jump between any two divisors is
147	the alternating sum of the two chart steps and the overlap step:
148	
149	`χ(D') − χ(D) = ΔS₀ + ΔS₁ − Δ𝒜`
150	
151	where each `Δ` is the difference of the corresponding dimensions.  Again no exactness
152	hypotheses.  This is the honest replacement for `ChiLedger.chi_add`. -/
153	theorem chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D D' : X.WeilDivisor)
154	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
155	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
156	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D')] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D')]
157	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D')] :
158	    chi k U₀ U₁ D' - chi k U₀ U₁ D =
159	      ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D') : ℤ) - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D))
160	      + ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D') : ℤ) - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D))
161	      - ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D') : ℤ)
162	          - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)) := by
163	  rw [chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D, chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D']
164	  ring
165	
166	/-- **A one-point bump does not change the sections over an open missing that point.**
167	`Γ(U, 𝒪(1·P + E)) = Γ(U, 𝒪(E))` when `P.point ∉ U`, because `Γ(U, −)` reads the divisor
168	only at primes meeting `U`.
169	
170	This is `LedgerClosure.sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap` with the overlap
171	`U₀ ⊓ U₁` generalised to an arbitrary open — the generalisation is what lets the same
172	computation be run at *all three* terms of the Čech count below. -/
173	theorem sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem (U : X.Opens)
174	    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U) (E : X.WeilDivisor) :
175	    sectionSub k U (pointDivisor P + E) = sectionSub k U E := by
176	  apply le_antisymm
177	  · intro x hx
178	    rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
179	    · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
180	    refine Or.inr fun Q hQ => ?_
181	    have hQP : Q ≠ P := fun h => hP (h ▸ hQ)
182	    rw [← add_pointDivisor_apply_of_ne E hQP]
183	    exact ((mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hx0).mp hx) Q hQ
184	  · exact sectionSub_mono k U (le_add_pointDivisor E P)
185	
186	/-- **The off-overlap χ-jump is exactly the ONE surviving chart step** — unconditionally.
187	
188	Let `P.point ∉ U₀`.  Then the bump `E ↦ 1·P + E` leaves both the `U₀` term and the
189	overlap term of `chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` untouched (`P.point ∉ U₀` and
190	`P.point ∉ U₀ ⊓ U₁`), so the entire χ-jump is carried by the `U₁` chart:
191	
192	`χ(1·P + E) − χ(E) = dim Γ(U₁, 𝒪(1·P+E)) − dim Γ(U₁, 𝒪(E))`.
193	
194	**This overturns the reading recorded at inbox `I-0449`/`I-0456`.**  Those items concluded
195	that `hbump` is *refuted* off the overlap, reasoning from `ChiLedger.chi_add`: that theorem
196	makes the χ-jump equal to the **overlap** local step, which is `0` off the overlap
197	(`LedgerClosure.finrank_localStepDom_eq_zero_of_notMem_overlap`), contradicting a jump of
198	`[κ(P):k] ≥ 1`.  Every step of that is valid, but the conclusion drawn from it is not:
199	what it actually shows is that **`chi_add`'s four exactness hypotheses are themselves
200	unsatisfiable off the overlap** — the audit observed exactly this ("`hbump` forces
201	`chi_add`'s window/connect/twist exactness hypotheses to FAIL") and then read it as a
202	statement about `hbump` rather than about `chi_add`.
203	
204	The truth is the opposite of the recorded one.  Off the overlap the two-set Čech complex
205	still computes χ, and it says the jump is the `U₁`-chart step — which is `≥ 0` and, under
206	approximation *on that chart*, exactly `[κ(P):k]`.  So `hbump` is **not** refutable off
207	the overlap; it is equivalent there to the one-chart step being full
208	(`bump_iff_chartStep_of_notMem_left`).  Correspondingly
209	`LedgerClosure.not_bump_of_notMem_overlap` is a true theorem whose hypothesis `hchiAdd`
210	is unsatisfiable at precisely the primes it is about, so it refutes nothing. -/
211	theorem chi_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_left (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
212	    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
213	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ E)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ E)]
214	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E)]
215	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ (pointDivisor P + E))]
216	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E))]
217	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) (pointDivisor P + E))] :
218	    chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) - chi k U₀ U₁ E =
219	      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E)) : ℤ)
220	        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ E) := by
221	  have hPinf : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens) := fun h => hP h.1
222	  rw [chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov E (pointDivisor P + E),
223	    sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem k U₀ hP E,
224	    sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) hPinf E]
225	  ring
226	
227	/-- **Off the overlap, the bump is EQUIVALENT to the one-chart step being full.**
228	
229	For `P.point ∉ U₀`, the bump statement `χ(1·P+E) = χ(E) + [κ(P):k]` holds if and only if
230	the `U₁`-chart section space grows by exactly `[κ(P):k]`.  Neither direction needs an
231	exactness hypothesis.
232	
233	So the residual content of `hbump` at an off-overlap prime is approximation **on the single
234	chart containing `P`** — a strictly local, strictly weaker demand than the overlap
235	approximation `hsurj` that `ChiLedger.chi_add_eq_residueDeg` requires, and in particular
236	not a contradiction.  This is the precise correction to `I-0449`. -/
237	theorem bump_iff_chartStep_of_notMem_left (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
238	    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
239	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ E)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ E)]
240	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E)]
241	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ (pointDivisor P + E))]
242	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E))]
243	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) (pointDivisor P + E))] :
244	    chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P ↔
245	      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E)) : ℤ)
246	        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ E) = residueDeg k P := by
247	  have h := chi_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_left k U₀ U₁ hcov hP E
248	  omega

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.ChiUnconditional
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.SectionBounds

universe u
open AlgebraicGeometry Adelic

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

/-- CONVERSE of `exists_bound_h1dim_eq_zero_of_charts`: its hypothesis is
EQUIVALENT to its conclusion, so it transports no information. -/
theorem converse_exists_bound (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (b : ℤ)
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
    (hvan : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D → h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0) :
    ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
        + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = (ell k D : ℤ) :=
  fun D hD => (h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts k U₀ U₁ hcov D).mp (hvan D hD)

/-- `ChartCountsDegree` is *literally* the ledger hypothesis of
`SectionBounds.degK_principal_eq_zero`; the "chart" version is an alpha-rename. -/
theorem chartCounts_is_hledger :
    ChartCountsDegree k U₀ U₁ ↔ (∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D) :=
  Iff.rfl

example (hcount : ChartCountsDegree k U₀ U₁) {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    degK k (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 :=
  degK_principal_eq_zero k U₀ U₁ hcount hg   -- old theorem accepts the "new" hypothesis verbatim

/-- The off-overlap theorems force `U₀ ≠ ⊤`, and a prime divisor sitting off `U₀`
means the complement of `U₀` contains a codim-1 point.  Meanwhile
`sectionSub k U₀ E` is then UNBOUNDED in the pole order along `P`:
every `L(m·P + E)` global section lands in it, for every `m ≥ 0`. -/
theorem chart_contains_all_pole_orders {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀)
    (E : X.WeilDivisor) (m : ℕ) :
    sectionSub k (⊤ : X.Opens) (m • pointDivisor P + E) ≤ sectionSub k U₀ E := by
  intro f hf
  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
  · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
  refine Or.inr fun Q hQ => ?_
  have hQP : Q ≠ P := fun h => hP (h ▸ hQ)
  have := (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf Q (by trivial)
  have hcoef : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from (m • pointDivisor P + E)) Q
      = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) Q := by
    simp [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.smul_apply, pointDivisor_apply_of_ne _ hQP]
  rwa [hcoef] at this
EOF

cat > /tmp/aud3.lean <<'EOF'
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.ChiUnconditional
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.SectionBounds

universe u
open AlgebraicGeometry Adelic

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

/-- CONVERSE of `exists_bound_h1dim_eq_zero_of_charts`: its hypothesis is
EQUIVALENT to its conclusion, so it transports no information. -/
theorem converse_exists_bound (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (b : ℤ)
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
    (hvan : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D → h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0) :
    ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
        + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = (ell k D : ℤ) :=
  fun D hD => (h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts k U₀ U₁ hcov D).mp (hvan D hD)

/-- `ChartCountsDegree` is *literally* the ledger hypothesis of
`SectionBounds.degK_principal_eq_zero`; the "chart" version is an alpha-rename. -/
theorem chartCounts_is_hledger :
    ChartCountsDegree k U₀ U₁ ↔ (∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D) :=
  Iff.rfl

example (hcount : ChartCountsDegree k U₀ U₁) {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    degK k (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 :=
  degK_principal_eq_zero k U₀ U₁ hcount hg   -- old theorem accepts the "new" hypothesis verbatim

/-- The off-overlap theorems force `U₀ ≠ ⊤`, and a prime divisor sitting off `U₀`
means the complement of `U₀` contains a codim-1 point.  Meanwhile
`sectionSub k U₀ E` is then UNBOUNDED in the pole order along `P`:
every `L(m·P + E)` global section lands in it, for every `m ≥ 0`. -/
theorem chart_contains_all_pole_orders {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀)
    (E : X.WeilDivisor) (m : ℕ) :
    sectionSub k (⊤ : X.Opens) (m • pointDivisor P + E) ≤ sectionSub k U₀ E := by
  intro f hf
  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
  · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
  refine Or.inr fun Q hQ => ?_
  have hQP : Q ≠ P := fun h => hP (h ▸ hQ)
  have := (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf Q (by trivial)
  have hcoef : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from (m • pointDivisor P + E)) Q
      = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) Q := by
    simp [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.smul_apply, pointDivisor_apply_of_ne _ hQP]
  rwa [hcoef] at this
EOF
